assays.assay_description: Paw licking events counted after intraplantar formalin (20 μL 2.5%) and immediate i.p. iboga analog treatment (30 mg/kg); recorded in phase 1 (up to 10 min) and phase 2 (10 min onwards), expressed as licking events per minute.

application_type.evidence: 70 μL iboga analog at a dose of 30 mg/kg intraperitoneally

setup_habituation.evidence: No pre-test apparatus habituation described for the paw-licking observation.

setup_restrain.evidence: Immediately after completion of the treatments, the non-invasive hyperalgesic and spontaneous behaviors of the treated mice were studied.

food_restriction.evidence: Mice were 'fed and watered freely throughout the day' in the home cage; no food in the observation apparatus.

water_restriction.evidence: Mice were 'fed and watered freely throughout the day' in the home cage; no water in the observation apparatus.

time_to_assay.evidence: Immediately after completion of the treatments, the non-invasive hyperalgesic and spontaneous behaviors of the treated mice were studied.

sample_size.evidence: A total of 60 animals were randomly assigned to ten experimental groups (n = 6)

outcomes.summary: Formalin increased paw licking events in both phases. Endo-iboga analogs (C2, C4, C6, C8) significantly reduced paw licking in phase 1 and phase 2 relative to formalin-treated mice, with the benzofuran Endo-analogs (C2, C4) somewhat better than natural C6/C8; Exo-analogs (C1, C3, C5, C7) had no significant effect.
outcomes.statistics: P < 0.05 vs formalin-treated group (One-way ANOVA with Tukey's test; exact F values not reported); Exo-analogs P > 0.05
outcomes.evidence: Endo-ibogaine and ibogamine derivatives from both the structural configuration (benzofuran/natural), i.e., C2, C4, C6 and C8, respectively, showed significant inhibition of paw licking events in comparison to formalin-treated group (P < 0.05)

B1_num_measures.evidence: Paw licking events (the same variable reported for phase 1 and phase 2).

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Mouse paw licking behavior was recorded in phase 1 (up to 10 min) and phase 2 (10 min onwards) after formalin infusion. The recorded events were measured as licking per minute for each mouse.

B4_ethological.evidence: Paw licking here is a nocifensive pain response, not a natural repertoire behaviour scored as such.

B5_social.evidence: No social component; animals tested individually.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Innate nociceptive response; no learning or memory component.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Licking events counted by observation; no automated classifier described.

B8_multivariate.evidence: Only One-/Two-way ANOVA were used; no dimensionality reduction.

E1_environment_type.evidence: Observation chamber not described in detail; standard formalin-test observation setting.

E6_spatial.evidence: Single observation chamber; no compartments described.

E7_social_context.evidence: Licking events measured per mouse individually.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water in the observation apparatus.

D1_continuity.evidence: Phase 1 and phase 2 licking were recorded within one continuous post-formalin observation period.

D2_session_duration.evidence: Phase 1 up to 10 min and phase 2 '10 min onwards'; total session length not explicitly stated as a number.

D3_recording_days.evidence: Licking recorded only on the day of formalin injection.

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug baseline paw-licking data reported.

D5_followup.evidence: Paw licking was only assessed acutely after treatment.

assays.assay_description: Radiant-heat tail-flick latency (s) measured in phase 1 and phase 2 after intraplantar formalin and immediate i.p. iboga analog treatment (30 mg/kg); three independent tail flicks per mouse per timepoint were averaged.

application_type.evidence: 70 μL iboga analog at a dose of 30 mg/kg intraperitoneally

setup_habituation.evidence: No pre-test habituation to the tail-flick apparatus described.

setup_restrain.evidence: The tail-flick apparatus and whether animals were restrained are not described.

food_restriction.evidence: Animals 'were fed and watered freely throughout the day' in the home cage; no food in the test apparatus.

water_restriction.evidence: Animals 'were fed and watered freely throughout the day' in the home cage; no water in the test apparatus.

time_to_assay.evidence: Immediately after completion of the treatments, the non-invasive hyperalgesic and spontaneous behaviors of the treated mice were studied.

sample_size.evidence: Iboga analogs were administered at a dose of 30 mg/kg via IP injection (n = 6)

outcomes.summary: Formalin shortened tail-flick latency; Endo-iboga analogs (C2, C4, C6, C8) restored tail-flick latency towards untreated control levels in both phase 1 and phase 2, while Exo-analogs (C1, C3, C5, C7) had no significant effect.
outcomes.statistics: P < 0.05 vs formalin-treated group (ANOVA with Tukey's test; exact F values not reported)
outcomes.evidence: Endo-iboga derivatives, namely, C2, C4, C6 and C8 showed significant hyperalgesic behavior (P < 0.05) in both phase 1 and phase 2, where both TFL (Figure 2C & 2D) and PWL (Figure 2E & 2F) were restored at an extent comparable to that of the untreated control mice.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Tail flick latency (seconds) is the single measure reported.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Tail flick latency reported separately for phase 1 and phase 2 of the post-formalin observation period.

B4_ethological.evidence: Tail flick is a spinal reflex, not an ethological behaviour.

E1_environment_type.evidence: Tail-flick radiant heat apparatus (standard nociception device).

E2_shelter.evidence: Definitionally absent in a tail-flick apparatus.

E7_social_context.evidence: Three independent tail flicks/mouse were recorded — individual testing.

D1_continuity.evidence: Tail flick latencies collected during the single post-formalin test day session (phases 1 and 2).

D2_session_duration.evidence: Duration of tail-flick measurement not explicitly stated; individual latency trials are brief.

D3_recording_days.evidence: Measured only on the day of formalin/iboga treatment.

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug tail-flick baseline data reported.

D5_followup.evidence: No tail-flick recording ≥24 h after drug.

assays.assay_description: Mice placed on a metal plate preheated to 52 ± 1 °C; paw withdrawal latency (time until the mouse licked or flicked its hind paw) recorded in phase 1 and phase 2 after formalin and immediate i.p. iboga analog treatment (30 mg/kg).

application_type.evidence: 70 μL iboga analog at a dose of 30 mg/kg intraperitoneally

setup_habituation.evidence: No pre-test habituation to the hot plate described.

setup_restrain.evidence: The hot plate test assessed the sensorimotor activity of each of the mice during painful stimuli when placed on a metal test plate preheated to 52 ± 1 °C.

food_restriction.evidence: Animals 'were fed and watered freely throughout the day' in the home cage; no food on the hot plate.

water_restriction.evidence: Animals 'were fed and watered freely throughout the day' in the home cage; no water on the hot plate.

time_to_assay.evidence: Immediately after completion of the treatments, the non-invasive hyperalgesic and spontaneous behaviors of the treated mice were studied.

sample_size.evidence: Iboga analogs were administered at a dose of 30 mg/kg via IP injection (n = 6)

outcomes.summary: Paw withdrawal latency on the hot plate was restored to near-control levels in both phases by Endo-iboga analogs (C2, C4, C6, C8) after formalin, whereas Exo-analogs (C1, C3, C5, C7) produced no significant change.
outcomes.statistics: P < 0.05 vs formalin-treated group (ANOVA with Tukey's test; exact F values not reported)
outcomes.evidence: Endo-iboga derivatives, namely, C2, C4, C6 and C8 showed significant hyperalgesic behavior (P < 0.05) in both phase 1 and phase 2, where both TFL (Figure 2C & 2D) and PWL (Figure 2E & 2F) were restored at an extent comparable to that of the untreated control mice.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Paw withdrawal latency (seconds) is the single reported measure.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Paw withdrawal latency reported separately for phase 1 and phase 2 of the post-formalin observation period.

B4_ethological.evidence: Paw withdrawal/licking latency is a reflexive nocifensive readout.

E7_social_context.evidence: each of the mice ... placed on a metal test plate — individual testing.

D1_continuity.evidence: Hot plate latencies collected on the single post-formalin test day.

D2_session_duration.evidence: Session duration not explicitly stated; latency trials are brief.

D3_recording_days.evidence: Measured only on the day of formalin/iboga treatment.

D5_followup.evidence: No hot-plate recording ≥24 h after drug.

assays.assay_description: Manual von Frey filaments (0.001–4 g) applied vertically to the lateral hind paw of unrestrained mice standing on a wire-mesh table under plexiglass cylinders; paw withdrawal threshold (g) recorded at 15 min, 30 min, 1 h, 6 h, 12 h and 24 h after formalin + i.p. iboga analog (30 mg/kg).

application_type.evidence: Iboga analogs were administered at a dose of 30 mg/kg via IP injection

setup_habituation.evidence: The mice were housed on a transparent plexiglass cylinder-enclosed wired mesh table for fifteen minutes before the experiment.

setup_restrain.evidence: Manual Von Frey monofilaments were applied vertically to the unrestrained animals with increasing force

food_restriction.evidence: No food in the plexiglass test cylinder; home-cage food was ad libitum.

water_restriction.evidence: No water in the plexiglass test cylinder; home-cage water was ad libitum.

time_to_assay.evidence: Paw withdrawal threshold (expressed in g) was recorded for a period of 15 min, 30 min, 1 h, 6 h, 12 h, 24 h post-formalin and iboga analog treatment.

sample_size.evidence: Iboga analogs were administered at a dose of 30 mg/kg via IP injection (n = 6)

outcomes.summary: Formalin significantly lowered paw withdrawal threshold at all timepoints (15 min–24 h). Endo-iboga analogs (C2, C4, C6, C8) prevented this decrease at every timepoint (absence of allodynia), while Exo-analogs (C1, C3, C5, C7) failed to show antiallodynic effects.
outcomes.statistics: Two-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's multiple comparison tests; P < 0.05 vs formalin at the given time points (exact F values not reported)
outcomes.evidence: However, Endo-iboga analogs (C2, C4, C6 and C8) treatment did not result in a significant decrease in the paw withdrawal threshold due to formalin injection at any observed time points, indicating the absence of allodynia.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Paw withdrawal threshold (expressed in g) was recorded

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: The 15 min–24 h timepoints are separate test sessions, not within-session temporal binning.

B4_ethological.evidence: Reflexive paw withdrawal to filament stimulation.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Manual Von Frey monofilaments were applied ... and the subsequent reaction of mice were recorded

E1_environment_type.evidence: transparent plexiglass cylinder-enclosed wired mesh table

E6_spatial.evidence: Single cylinder compartment on the mesh table.

E7_social_context.evidence: Individual mice tested in the plexiglass cylinders.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food/water in the testing cylinder.

D2_session_duration.evidence: Duration of each von Frey measurement session not explicitly stated; filament application is brief.

D3_recording_days.evidence: Timepoints from 15 min to 24 h post-formalin span two calendar days.

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug von Frey baseline data reported.

D5_followup.evidence: 24 h post-formalin and iboga analog treatment timepoint recorded.

assays.assay_description: Circular open field (40 cm radius, 17 cm high opaque walls); mice placed in the centre and allowed to explore for 5 min; distance travelled and mean speed tracked with ANY-Maze, recorded before treatment and 24 h after formalin + i.p. iboga analog (30 mg/kg).

application_type.evidence: Iboga analogs were injected at 30 mg/kg dose via IP injection

setup_habituation.evidence: No separate habituation session to the open field described (a pre-treatment test recording was performed, but data were collected).

setup_restrain.evidence: The animals were set free to the circular open field arena ... mice were placed at the center and allowed to explore the field for 5 minutes.

food_restriction.evidence: No food in the open field arena; home-cage food ad libitum.

water_restriction.evidence: No water in the open field arena; home-cage water ad libitum.

outcomes.summary: Formalin reduced distance travelled and mean speed measured 24 h later; Endo-iboga epimers (C2, C4, C6, C8) restored locomotor activity to near-control levels, whereas Exo-analogs (C1, C3, C5, C7) did not. The analogs themselves produced no locomotor impairment.
outcomes.statistics: P < 0.05 vs formalin-treated group (ANOVA with Tukey's test; exact F values not reported)
outcomes.evidence: After 24 h of formalin treatment, there was a decrease observed in the measurement of locomotor activity including mean speed (MS, measured in m/s) (Figure 4E) and distance travelled (DT, measured in m) (Figure 4C), which was not evident in the Endo-iboga epimers (C2, C4, C6, and C8)-treated groups.

assays.assay_description: Wooden EPM (two open arms 30 × 5 cm, two closed arms 30 × 5 × 15 cm, elevated 40 cm); 5-min test; number of open-arm entries and time spent in open arms scored by ANY-Maze, recorded before treatment and 24 h after formalin + i.p. iboga analog (30 mg/kg).

application_type.evidence: Iboga analogs were injected at 30 mg/kg dose intraperitoneally

setup_habituation.evidence: No separate non-recorded habituation to the maze described.

setup_restrain.evidence: Each animal was placed at the center of the maze facing any of the open arms.

food_restriction.evidence: No food on the maze; home-cage food ad libitum.

water_restriction.evidence: No water on the maze; home-cage water ad libitum.

time_to_assay.evidence: the locomotor activity, anxiety-like response and inflammatory mediators were measured 24 h posttreatment.

sample_size.evidence: Iboga analogs were injected at 30 mg/kg dose intraperitoneally (n = 6)

outcomes.summary: Formalin significantly reduced open-arm entries and time spent in the open arms 24 h later; Endo-iboga analogs (C2, C4, C6, C8) preserved open-arm exploration (anxiolytic-like effect), whereas Exo-analogs failed to counteract the anxiogenic effect of formalin.
outcomes.statistics: P < 0.05 vs formalin-treated group; Exo-analogs P > 0.05 (ANOVA with Tukey's test; exact F values not reported)
outcomes.evidence: After receiving formalin, the animal's movement in the open arm the plus maze was restricted significantly (P < 0.05) ... while the Endo-iboga analog (C2, C4, C6 and C8) therapy clearly preserved the animal's ability to travel around the open arm of the plus labyrinth (Figure 5C & 5E).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Important measurements of anxiolytic behavior included the number of entries (NE) and time spent in seconds (TS) in the open arm.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Totals over the 5-min session; no within-session time course.

B4_ethological.evidence: Open-arm entries and time are spatial measures, not ethological acts.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Innate avoidance test; no learning requirement.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: the exploration of mice was video recorded considering the central point by ANY-Maze software (position tracking).

E2_shelter.evidence: EPM closed arms are part of the apparatus design, not a shelter (per rubric).

E4_nesting.evidence: Definitionally absent in an elevated plus maze.

E6_spatial.evidence: EPM arms are open-ended extensions of a central platform (scored 0 per rubric).

E7_social_context.evidence: Each animal was placed at the center of the maze (tested individually).

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water in the maze.

D1_continuity.evidence: Before and after receiving treatments with formalin and iboga analogs, the movements of the mice in the maze's open and closed arms were observed.

D2_session_duration.evidence: Through a test period of 5 minutes, the exploration of mice was video recorded

D3_recording_days.evidence: Pre-treatment recording day plus the 24 h post-treatment recording day.

D4_baseline.evidence: (B). Number of entries in the open arm before formalin or iboga treatment. (D). Time spent in the open arm before formalin/iboga treatment.

judge_notes: Excluded the rat ECG/QTc study (Section 2.9) — purely physiological recording, not a behavioural assay; also excluded in silico docking, MTT cytotoxicity, ELISA/immunoblot, oxidative-stress and histology endpoints.

Split the tail flick test and the hot plate (paw withdrawal latency) test into two assays: they use different apparatuses, stimuli and protocols (radiant heat to tail vs. 52 °C metal plate) despite two candidates merging them into one 'thermal nociception' entry.
Paw licking scored as 1 behavioural measure (same variable reported for phase 1 and phase 2), overriding a candidate that counted the two phases as separate measures.

B2 scored Yes for the formalin-phase assays (paw licking, tail flick, hot plate) because data are reported separately for phase 1 (0–10 min) and phase 2 (>10 min) of the same post-injection observation period, and licking was quantified per minute; B2 scored No for von Frey where the 15 min–24 h timepoints are separate sessions.
D2 scored 0 with low confidence for the formalin-phase and von Frey assays because no explicit total session length is given (overriding a candidate that assigned 15–60 min to paw licking).
D3 for von Frey scored 2-7 days because the 15 min–24 h timepoint series necessarily spans two calendar days; D5 Yes due to the 24 h timepoint.
D5 scored Yes for OFT and EPM: the paper states locomotor and anxiety-like responses were measured 24 h post-treatment (overriding one candidate who scored No).
Mouse sex is never stated ('Swiss albino mice, aged 6-8 weeks'); the word 'male' in the ethics paragraph is an OCR artifact of the ministry name, so sex = not_reported.
day_night_flipped set to not_reported (only '12-hour light-dark cycle' is given, without direction or testing phase), overriding one candidate's 'no'.
